newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares ends lower in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares ends lower in nervous trade.

text.p: Share prices finished sharply lower for the second straight day on Friday as jittery investors cut their exposures amid mounting anxiety over political stability, brokers said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index fell 50.09 points, or 1.51 percent, to a provisional 3,256.96.

"It's a toss up," said a trader. "Anything can happen on Monday." He said the market was trying to discount the possible arrest of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, whose Congress party's support is vital for the minority coalition government.
Rao's lawyer said on Thursday that he expected the former Congress party president to be arrested on Monday, when Rao has been ordered to appear in a Delhi court in a conspiracy case.
"The Congress may have to rethink its support to the United Front government," said Vijay Pandya, director at Classic Share and Stock Brokers. "That's why the market is so grim."
"The relationship comes under strain," said Bharat Iyer, strategist at UBS Securities.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index shed 13.37 points, or 1.39 percent, to 945.64 and the CRISIL-500 index 9.64 points, or 1.50 percent, to 632.59, both provisional closings.

Traders said the political fears added to the market's other woes like slowing earnings growth forecast. The falling market posed a threat to domestic and foreign new issues planned by many companies.
SBI stock fell 8.25 rupees to 251 at the BSE. The bank is expected to price its $400 million global depositary receipt issue on October 3.

ACC fell 42 rupees to 1,763, TELCO 6.50 to 448.25, M&M 8.25 to 319.75, Reliance 7.75 to 186, L&T 6.25 to 233, Grasim 7.25 to 411, Hindalco 9.75 to 685.25, Arvind Mills 4.0 to 117.50 and TISCO 2.75 to 167.25.
